questions.q: What are the three purposes of the 30-day plan?
options: To let the rhythm become familiar, work through the cards without recreating burnout, and give optional sessions and testing the time they need
To become a different person, finish every card, and plan the next retreat
To review the book, re-read the sessions, and write a report
questions.explanation: Day 30 is a review, not a deadline. Philippians 1:6: he who began a good work will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ, not on Day 30.

questions.q: What is the one thing that does not wait for the calendar?
options: Reading Chapter 16 and acting on it if any warning sign from Chapters 4 or 5 applies
questions.explanation: Safety and professional help take priority over every week of the plan.

questions.q: What is the daily minimum for the month?
options: The rhythm from Session Ten's card; if that rhythm is weekly, a psalm and a few minutes of quiet on the days you can
questions.explanation: When you miss, resume the next day without compensation or guilt.

questions.q: What is Week 1 for, and what should you NOT do in it?
options: Writing the rule; do not rest
Session Six; do not test anything
The Jethro conversation; do not tell anyone
Landing softly, expecting the dip, doing little; do not pronounce a verdict, announce conclusions, redesign your life, or begin the rule yet
questions.explanation: Day 1 is reading Chapter 13 and sorting the cards. Tell your support person you are home: one conversation, not a report.

questions.q: In which week is the rule of life written?
questions.explanation: Week 2 is doing (the cards leave the pile), Week 3 is shaping (the rule), Week 4 is settling (review, and Session Six only if its conditions are met).

questions.q: What does the chapter say to readers who reach Day 30 having done only a fraction of the plan?
options: The plan does not expire; begin at the next unfinished step that matters, and recognise that what you did do may have been the important part
questions.explanation: One rhythm kept on some days, one appointment, one conversation: those are not a fraction of the plan. They are the plan, in the form your month allowed. Resume.

reflection: Grace received: where did you notice help, kindness, provision, truth, rest, or God's presence during the month?
The intention: read it again. What has become clearer, and what still needs attention?
The rhythm: how often did you keep it? What helped it happen, and what repeatedly prevented it?
The next pause: what will it be, and when will you book it?
